questions.question: What does NoSQL stand for?
Who first introduced the term 'NoSQL' in 1998?
Which of the following is NOT a category of NoSQL databases?
Which NoSQL database type is best suited for social networks due to its relationship modeling?
What does the CAP theorem state?
options: A. A distributed system can guarantee Consistency, Availability, and Partition-tolerance simultaneously
B. A distributed system can guarantee at most two of Consistency, Availability, and Partition-tolerance
C. Consistency is always preferred over Availability in distributed systems
D. Only Partition-tolerance and Consistency can coexist

questions.question: In the CAP theorem, what does 'Availability' mean?
options: A. All copies have the same value
B. Reads and writes always succeed
C. The system operates despite network failures
D. Data is replicated to multiple nodes

questions.question: In the CAP theorem, what does 'Partition-tolerance' mean?
options: A. All copies have the same value
B. Reads and writes always succeed
C. System properties hold even when network failures prevent some machines from communicating
D. Data is sharded across multiple nodes

questions.question: What is 'eventual consistency' in NoSQL systems?
options: A. Data is always immediately consistent across all nodes
B. When no updates occur for a long period, all nodes will eventually become consistent
C. Data is only consistent on the master node
D. Consistency is never guaranteed in NoSQL systems

questions.question: What does ACID stand for in database transactions?
What does BASE stand for in NoSQL consistency models?
options: A. Basic Availability, Strict-state, Eventual consistency
B. Basically Available, Soft-state, Eventual consistency
C. Basically Available, Strong-state, Exact consistency
D. Basic Availability, Stable-state, Eventual consistency

questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of NoSQL over relational databases?
options: B. Rich JOIN and GROUP BY operations
C. Horizontal scalability and no schema requirement

questions.question: Which scaling approach does NoSQL favor?
options: A. Vertical scaling (making a single machine more powerful)
B. Horizontal scaling (adding more smaller/cheaper servers)
C. Temporal scaling (faster processing over time)
